label: prf:baryon-product-from-alt
title: Proof of baryon product from alt
html:
Proof. By Schur–Weyl duality at level n = 3 in three dimensions (Schur–Weyl mass decomposition), the \mathrm{S}_3-module

  V \;:=\; \bigotimes_{k=1}^{3}\, T_{c_k}\mathbf{C}
  \;\cong\; R\,\langle dc_1/dz,\ dc_2/dz,\ dc_3/dz\rangle

decomposes into isotypic components labelled by partitions of 3:

  V \;\cong\; V_{(3)} \;\oplus\; V_{(1,1,1)} \;\oplus\; V_{(2,1)}
  \;=\; \mathrm{Sym}^3 \;\oplus\; \mathrm{Alt}^3 \;\oplus\; \mathrm{Std}^{\oplus 2}.

The dimensions are \dim_R V_{(3)} = 1, \dim_R V_{(1,1,1)} = 1, \dim_R V_{(2,1)} = 2, summing to 4. However, since V is the rank-3 permutation representation of \mathrm{S}_3, we have V \cong V_{(3)} \oplus V_{(2,1)}. The rank-1 alternating piece sits inside the exterior cube \Lambda^3 V. The relevant isotype is therefore the top exterior power.

By the Frobenius character formula (Frobenius universal) applied to \mathrm{S}_3, the projector onto the sign isotype of any \mathrm{S}_3-module W is

  \pi_{\mathrm{Alt}}
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{|\mathrm{S}_3|} \sum_{\sigma \in \mathrm{S}_3}
    \mathrm{sgn}(\sigma)\, \sigma
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{6}\bigl(
    \mathrm{id} - (12) - (13) - (23) + (123) + (132)
  \bigr).

Applied to dc_1/dz \otimes dc_2/dz \otimes dc_3/dz \in V^{\otimes 3}, this projector yields the antisymmetrisation

  \pi_{\mathrm{Alt}}\bigl(dc_1/dz \otimes dc_2/dz \otimes dc_3/dz\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{6} \sum_{\sigma \in \mathrm{S}_3}
    \mathrm{sgn}(\sigma)\,
    \bigotimes_{k=1}^{3} dc_{\sigma(k)}/dz.

Under the canonical isomorphism \Lambda^3 V \cong R, the antisymmetrised tensor maps to the wedge product

  (dc_1/dz) \wedge (dc_2/dz) \wedge (dc_3/dz).

Evaluated on the diagonal vector \bigl((dc_k/dz)\,e_k\bigr)_{k=1}^{3} with R-basis \{e_1, e_2, e_3\}, this yields

  \bigl((dc_1/dz)\,e_1\bigr) \wedge \bigl((dc_2/dz)\,e_2\bigr)
    \wedge \bigl((dc_3/dz)\,e_3\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \Bigl(\prod_{k=1}^{3} \frac{dc_k}{dz}\Bigr)\,
  e_1 \wedge e_2 \wedge e_3
  \;\longmapsto\;
  \prod_{k=1}^{3} \frac{dc_k}{dz}

under the identification e_1 \wedge e_2 \wedge e_3 \mapsto 1. This product structure arises solely from multilinearity of \wedge.

The squared Vandermonde of the colour-tube roots equals the cubic's discriminant (color-tube cubic):

  V_3(c_1, c_2, c_3)^2
  \;=\;
  \prod_{1 \leq i < j \leq 3} (c_i - c_j)^2
  \;=\;
  \Delta(z)
  \;\in\; R[z].

Using implicit differentiation dc_k/dz = -(\partial F/\partial z)|_{(z, c_k)} \big/ (\partial F/\partial c)|_{(z, c_k)} and the resultant identity J(z) := \prod_{k=1}^{3} (\partial F/\partial c)|_{(z, c_k)} = \pm\, \Delta(z), the Alt-isotype representative satisfies

  \prod_{k=1}^{3} \frac{dc_k}{dz}
  \;=\;
  (-1)^{3}\,
  \frac{V_3(c_1, c_2, c_3)}{J(z)}
  \;=\;
  \pm\,\frac{V_3(c_1, c_2, c_3)}{\Delta(z)}.

Thus we obtain

  \Bigl(\prod_{k=1}^{3} \frac{dc_k}{dz}\Bigr)^{2}
  \;=\;
  \frac{V_3(c_1, c_2, c_3)^2}{\Delta(z)^2}
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{\Delta(z)}
  \;\in\; R(z),

which is manifestly R-rational. \square

The sum \sum_k dc_k/dz projects onto the trivial isotype V_{(3)} as the integrand for a symmetric trion. The baryon sits in the antisymmetric colour singlet \mathrm{Alt}^3, selecting the wedge product. This algebraic selection requires no input from the Picard–Lefschetz machinery. Both the Vandermonde and \pi_{\mathrm{Alt}} are defined over R; the baryon integrand evaluation remains R-rational until we apply the archimedean fibre functor \tau.

This algebraic choice of the sign block, combined with the scalar weight w_\lambda from the Markov trace (categorical mass as Markov trace), fully determines the baryon integrand \lambda_{\mathrm{baryon}}.

Scope of the selection — derived versus input. Two claims must be kept apart. That \mathrm{Alt}^3 is a genuinely non-trivial one-dimensional representation is derived: the monodromy of the color-tube cubic F around its discriminant is the full \mathrm{S}_3, computed exactly over R = \mathbb{Q}[z] (irreducibility over \mathbb{C}(z) gives transitivity; the depressed quadratic is coprime to \Delta, so every one of the six simple branch points carries a transposition, and a transitive subgroup of \mathrm{S}_3 with a transposition is \mathrm{S}_3) and confirmed at 50 digits by transporting the three sheets around all six branch points — every loop returns a transposition and the six generate \mathrm{S}_3 (monodromy witness). Had the group been only A_3, the sign line would coincide with the trivial one and selecting \mathrm{Alt}^3 would carry no information; the surjectivity onto \{\pm 1\} rules that out. What remains an input — not derived from the categorical substrate — is that the physical baryon occupies \mathrm{Alt}^3 rather than the trivial or standard isotype: this is the color-singlet (confinement) condition. Stating the occupation as a derivation would conflate an invariant of the fibre (the non-trivial sign line, which the geometry supplies) with the channel of the state (which it does not), and is the standing open item.
